semis.name: Semiconductors net of the Nasdaq-100 (SOXX less its walked-forward beta times QQQ)

normal.model: normal quantile at the RiskMetrics volatility (lambda 0.94)

filtered.model: walked-forward 1% quantile of standardized returns at the RiskMetrics volatility

scenarios_method: Each scenario states three moves: the Nasdaq-100, the AI names beyond the Nasdaq-100, and the long yield. Nasdaq leg: each name's loading on QQQ times the Nasdaq-100 move. AI leg: each name's loading on the book's own daily return less QQQ's (today's weights), times the scenario's AI move; the scenario's AI basket is these nine names, so the whole book's loading on this leg is about 1 by construction and a name's is its share of that. Rates leg: each name's loading on the 20-year par bond's return, given the other two, times the bond's repriced return for the yield move (duration and convexity at today's 20-year yield). Loadings are exponentially weighted least squares, half-life 126 days, on all three at once; a name with under two years of history leans on its prior. Before v0.47 the AI move was put on semiconductors net of the Nasdaq-100, a factor this book loads on negatively, so an AI sell-off raised the book and an AI rally lowered it.

correlation.definition: 63-day exponentially weighted correlation of daily returns, book vs the 20-year par bond

limitations: Today's weights applied to history: the record is what this book would have done, not what anyone held.
GOOG (class C) stands in for GOOGL; the two trade within a fraction of a percent of each other.
SPCX has traded since June 12, 2026. Before that its weight is spread over the other names pro rata, and its betas lean on TSLA's until it has two years of its own.

The rates factor is a 20-year par bond rebuilt from the Treasury's daily par yields, a TLT proxy with duration about 12 against TLT's 16. Cash is proxied by the 2-year yield (older Treasury files here carry 2, 10 and 20 years only). That overstates what idle cash earned when the curve was steep (2021 and 2022) and understates it when the curve was inverted (2023 and 2024); a bill rate is the right series and is not in use yet.

The drawdown cap is read from a constant-volatility simulation (geometric Brownian motion, 4,000 paths) at an assumed drift. It has no volatility clustering, no jumps and no change in correlation, so the 25% is a modelled 95th percentile under those assumptions and not a stop: a real drawdown at that size can be deeper. From v0.44 the page shows the size under fat tails, the book's own days in runs, volatility that moves, no equity premium and higher volatility (sensitivity.py), and whether the cap held in the walk-forward. The call still uses the constant-volatility number.
The menu's rows are at or inside each limit exactly, in 5% steps of the short. The exact minimum short is reported beside the logged row; the logged row is the decision.
Hedge legs are measured as futures: their returns are in excess of cash. No transaction costs, no margin, no borrow.
Ten years of daily data hold one bear market (2022) and two fast crashes (2020, 2025); the tail numbers are only as wide as that record, which is why the most cautious of three methods governs.

validation.source: yennanliu/finance_data on GitHub (Yahoo Finance via yfinance); split-adjusted closes, dividends on ex-dates

rules.stale: every file ends on the session before today in New York, and on the same day as the others
rules.jump: no one-day fall beyond 30% or rise beyond 45% without a recorded split
rules.cross_check: the newest close within 1% of a second source

cross_check.note: Yahoo answered; the mirror is built from Yahoo, so this checks the copy against its origin, not the origin itself

sources.treasury: US Treasury daily par yield curve rates (home.treasury.gov)

findings: Measured on the nine names' own daily prices from 2017-01-04 to 2026-11-24, the book at 1.00x runs 35% volatility, a one-month 95% expected shortfall of 25.7% (the most cautious of historical 14.9%, filtered 25.7% and Student-t 22.4%) and a one-year 95% drawdown of 51%, against limits of 12%, 20% and 25%.

The limits allow 0.47x (shortfall), 0.58x (volatility) and 0.44x (drawdown); the drawdown cap binds, so the book's size is 0.44x. Keeping every name at full size instead takes a Nasdaq-100 futures short of 98% of NAV.

Exposures: Nasdaq-100 beta 1.17 (broad market 1.61 now, 1.35 over ten years), semis net of the market -0.31, rates -0.16. 86% of the variance is the market and 13% is stock-specific: effective independent bets 1.3 of nine.

Hedges walked forward from 2017-07-06: a Nasdaq-100 short at the measured beta cut the variance 90% and turned 2022 from -42% to -0.2%; the long bond held only when its correlation said it hedged cut it 3% (2022 -45%), and a standing 30% long bond 0% (2022 -48%).
Stock-bond correlation (63-day, book against the 20-year bond): -0.05, state neutral. On the book's worst 5% of days since 2022 the bond rose 55% of the time.
The one-day 99% VaR, backtested on the book: a normal model at today's volatility was breached 56 times against 24 expected (p 0.000); filtered historical simulation 16 against 22 (p 0.19).

rows.label: The engine's model
rows.what: constant volatility, normal shocks, the assumed drift

rows.label: Fat tails
rows.what: the same volatility and drift; shocks from a Student-t with 5 degrees of freedom, each day independent

rows.label: The book's own days, in runs
rows.what: the same volatility and drift; the book's own daily moves since 2017, redrawn in runs averaging 21 days, so bad days stay together

rows.label: Volatility that moves
rows.what: the same starting volatility and drift; each day's variance follows the last day's move, so a bad week raises what comes after

rows.label: No equity premium
rows.what: the engine's model with drift equal to cash: nothing is assumed to be earned for the risk

rows.label: Today's volatility
rows.what: the engine's model at the volatility of the last few weeks (53%) in place of the factor model's (35%)

rows.label: The worst year's volatility
rows.what: the engine's model at the book's highest one-year realized volatility (42%)

settings.label: the most cautious of the three (filtered)
its months rescaled to today's volatility
a fat-tailed curve at the model's volatility

sensitivity.note: Each row changes one thing and holds the rest. The call is unchanged by any of this; it is how far to trust the size.
